headline: Bathroom Remodeling Factors Buyers Should Compare
articleBody: Bathroom remodeling is often more code-sensitive than it appears because it combines plumbing, electrical, ventilation, waterproofing, and slip-resistance concerns in a small space. California building and plumbing standards require properly vented fixtures, approved waterproofing in wet areas, and safe electrical placement around tubs, showers, and sinks. The CDC and EPA both emphasize that moisture control is essential because persistent dampness can contribute to mold and indoor air quality problems. In Los Angeles County, older bathrooms often need updated exhaust fans, grounded outlets, and improved shower pan construction before premium finishes are installed. Homeowners comparing contractors should ask whether the proposed scope includes demolition to the studs, inspection of hidden rot, and replacement of supply and drain lines if corrosion is found. Tile, grout, and backer board choices matter because durability depends on correct substrate preparation as much as on the finish product. Buyers should also confirm whether the contractor will provide documentation of waterproofing products and installation methods, since many manufacturer warranties depend on strict installation compliance. From a scheduling standpoint, bathroom remodels can be delayed by lead times for custom vanities, tile, and glass enclosures, so the contractor’s procurement process is an important part of the bid. The most reliable bids are those that specify exactly which fixtures, finishes, and wall conditions are included and which are allowances or exclusions.
